description: KnockoutNotes Clinical Content & Question Review Register

records.topic: Sepsis Antimicrobial Timing (4-tier stratification)
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign International Guidelines 2026; Prescott HC et al., Intensive Care Med 2026; Evans L et al., Crit Care Med 2021
records.notes: Verified 4-tier timing: immediate (<1 h) for shock/probable sepsis; <3 h for possible sepsis without shock; defer/monitor if unlikely. Clarified in study-data.js and content-config.js.

records.topic: Beta-Lactam Extended/Continuous Infusion & PK/PD Dosing
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026; BLING III Trial (JAMA 2024); Roberts JA et al., Lancet Infect Dis
records.notes: Verified initial loading dose followed by extended/continuous infusion to optimize fT > MIC in capillary leak and hyperdynamic states.

records.topic: Initial Resuscitation Fluid Volume (30 mL/kg Balanced Crystalloid)
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 / 2021; SMART Trial (NEJM 2018); CLOVERS Trial (NEJM 2023)
records.notes: Corrected wording: 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid within 3 hours is a suggested starting point (conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence), NOT a rigid universal mandate.

records.topic: Vasopressor Hierarchy (Norepinephrine, Vasopressin 0.03 U/min)
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 / 2021; VASST Trial (NEJM 2008); CENSER Trial (AJRCCM 2019)
records.notes: Verified Norepinephrine first-line (peripheral infusion safe in large vein pending CVC); Vasopressin 0.03 U/min fixed adjunct (not titrated); Dobutamine for myocardial dysfunction.

records.topic: Age-Stratified Perfusion Pressure Targets (Standard vs Older Adults)
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026; 65 Trial (JAMA 2020); SEPSISPAM (NEJM 2014)
records.notes: Verified standard adult MAP target >= 65 mmHg; clarified initial conservative target 60-65 mmHg for older adults (>= 65 yrs) as a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence.

records.topic: Adjunctive Corticosteroid Therapy in Refractory Septic Shock
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 / 2021; ADRENAL Trial (NEJM 2018); APROCCHSS Trial (NEJM 2018)
records.notes: Verified IV hydrocortisone 200 mg/day (50 mg q6h or continuous infusion) conditional for shock requiring NE >= 0.25 mcg/kg/min for >= 4h. ACTH stimulation test is not recommended.

records.topic: Biomarker Role of Procalcitonin (PCT) in Stewardship vs Initiation
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 / 2021; SAPS Trial (Lancet Infect Dis 2016); PRORATA Trial
records.notes: Verified recommendation AGAINST using PCT to decide whether to initiate antimicrobials; verified suggestion for PCT-guided de-escalation and cessation (drop >= 80% or < 0.25 mcg/L).

records.topic: Active Fluid De-resuscitation Post-Shock Resolution
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026; ROSE Framework; FACTT Trial (NEJM 2006)
records.notes: Verified conditional recommendation supporting active fluid removal (conservative fluid management, loop diuretics, or ultrafiltration) once hemodynamic stability is achieved.

records.topic: qSOFA Role in Sepsis Screening vs Diagnosis
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 / 2021; Sepsis-3 Consensus (Singer M et al., JAMA 2016)
records.notes: Verified recommendation AGAINST qSOFA as a single standalone screening tool due to low sensitivity; validated screening systems (NEWS, MEWS, SIRS) preferred.

records.topic: Stress Ulcer Prophylaxis (SUP) Indications in Sepsis
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 / 2021; PEPTIC Trial (JAMA 2020); REVISE Trial (NEJM 2024)
records.notes: Verified recommendation against routine SUP in sepsis without specific risk factors; indicated if mechanical ventilation >= 48 hours or coagulopathy is present.

records.topic: Peripheral Norepinephrine Safety & Extravasation Antidote
records.sourceAndEdition: Marino's The ICU Book 4th ed.; Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021/2026; Loubani OM et al., Ann Pharmacother
records.notes: Verified peripheral administration safety criteria (vein >= antecubital/forearm, <= 72 h); verified extravasation rescue protocol: phentolamine 5-10 mg in 10-15 mL saline subcutaneous infiltration + topical 2% nitroglycerin paste.

records.topic: Pediatric Endotracheal Tube Sizing & Airway Anatomy
records.sourceAndEdition: A Practice of Anesthesia for Infants and Children (Cote CJ et al., 6th ed.), Table 42-6; APAGBI Guidelines
records.notes: Verified cuffed ETT formula: (Age/4) + 3.5; uncuffed Cole formula: (Age/4) + 4.0; depth formula: (Age/2) + 12 cm or ID x 3. Verified leak test at 15-25 cmH2O.

records.topic: Arterial Blood Gas Delta-Gap & Mixed Acid-Base Interpretation
records.sourceAndEdition: Clinical Physiology of Acid-Base and Electrolyte Disorders (Rose BD 5th ed.); Marino's The ICU Book
records.notes: Verified delta-ratio [Delta AG / Delta HCO3]: < 0.4-0.8 (mixed high AG + normal AG acidosis); 0.8-1.2/1.6 (pure high AG acidosis); > 1.6-2.0 (mixed high AG acidosis + metabolic alkalosis or preexisting hyperbicarbonatemia).

records.topic: Cockcroft-Gault Creatinine Clearance Weight Rules
records.sourceAndEdition: Cockcroft DW, Gault MH, Nephron 1976; FDA Guidance for Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function
records.notes: Verified weight selection logic: TBW if underweight (< IBW); IBW if normal weight; Adjusted Body Weight (ABW = IBW + 0.4*(TBW-IBW)) if obese (BMI >= 30 or TBW > 120% IBW). Female factor 0.85.

records.topic: MELD-Na (2016 OPTN/UNOS Consensus Revision)
records.sourceAndEdition: Kamath PS et al., Hepatology 2007; OPTN/UNOS Policy 9.1 Allocation of Deceased Donor Livers 2016
records.notes: Verified 2016 OPTN formula: MELD(i) bounded [6, 40]; if MELD(i) > 11, MELD-Na = MELD(i) + 1.32*(137 - Na) - [0.033 * MELD(i) * (137 - Na)], with serum Na bounded [125, 137] mEq/L and final score bounded [6, 40].

records.topic: ARDS Lung-Protective Mechanical Ventilation & Predicted Body Weight
records.sourceAndEdition: ARDSNet (NEJM 2000); ESICM ARDS Guidelines (Intensive Care Med 2023)
records.notes: Verified tidal volume 4-8 mL/kg of PBW (never actual body weight); plateau pressure <= 30 cmH2O; driving pressure <= 14-15 cmH2O; prone positioning >= 16 h/day for PaO2/FiO2 < 150.

records.topic: Propofol Infusion Syndrome (PRIS) Risk & Monitoring Limits
records.sourceAndEdition: Marino's The ICU Book; Krajcova A et al., Crit Care 2015; Mirrakhimov AE et al., Crit Care Res Pract
records.notes: Verified threshold warning: doses > 4-5 mg/kg/h (> 67-83 mcg/kg/min) or duration > 48 hours; monitoring markers: refractory metabolic lactic acidosis, hyperkalemia, hypertriglyceridemia, rhabdomyolysis, and Brugada-like ECG pattern.

records.topic: Extracorporeal Blood Purification & Hemoadsorption in Sepsis
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign International Guidelines 2026 (Intensive Care Med 2026; doi:10.1007/s00134-026-08361-1); SSC 2021 (Crit Care Med 2021;49(11):e1063–e1143); EUPHRATES Trial (JAMA 2018;320(14):1455-1463); CytoSorb-Sepsis Trial (Crit Care 2017;21:247)
records.notes: QUALIFIED: SSC 2021/2026 guidelines suggest against routine blood purification/hemoadsorption outside clinical trials. Content qualified to distinguish surrogate cytokine reduction from unproven patient-centered clinical benefit and detail potential harms. Final institutional adoption requires clinician adjudication.
records.originalClaimOrProblem: Cytokine adsorption and polymyxin B hemoperfusion were listed as blood purification technologies without explicit distinction between surrogate biomarker clearance and patient-centered clinical endpoints or antibiotic adsorption risks.
records.reviewFinding: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021/2026 guidelines suggest against using polymyxin B hemoperfusion or other blood purification techniques outside clinical trials. Surrogate cytokine reduction has not translated to improved mortality or organ-failure-free days in multicenter RCTs (EUPHRATES, CytoSorb-Sepsis), with risks of hydrophilic antibiotic adsorption.
records.actionTaken: Enhanced study curriculum to distinguish established RRT (AEIOU criteria) from investigational sorbents, explicitly highlight guideline recommendations against routine use, and detail potential harms (antimicrobial clearance, thrombocytopenia).
records.remainingUncertainty: Subgroup efficacy in specific endotoxin activity ranges (EAA 0.60-0.89) remains under investigational trial evaluation (TIGRIS trial). Potential harms from non-selective antibiotic/platelet adsorption require clinician adjudication when considering compassionate off-label use.

records.topic: Pediatric Sepsis Refractory Shock Hydrocortisone Dosing & Criteria
records.sourceAndEdition: Pediatric Surviving Sepsis Campaign International Guidelines (Weiss SL et al., Pediatr Crit Care Med 2020; 21(2):e52–e106 / Intensive Care Med 2020; 46(Suppl 1):10–67)
records.notes: QUALIFIED: Pediatric SSC 2020 guidelines suggest IV hydrocortisone only for fluid-refractory, catecholamine-resistant shock (weak recommendation, low certainty). Explicitly qualified with pediatric-specific dosing (1-2 mg/kg/dose q6h or 50-100 mg/m2/day continuous, max 200 mg/d), anti-recommendation in responsive shock, and caution against adult fixed dosing. Human clinician sign-off required for unit protocols.
records.originalClaimOrProblem: Hydrocortisone was listed for pediatric septic shock without clear demarcation of guideline recommendation strength, responsive shock anti-recommendation, or explicit capping at adult maximum doses.
records.reviewFinding: Pediatric Surviving Sepsis Campaign (pSSC 2020) guidelines suggest hydrocortisone ONLY for fluid-refractory, catecholamine-resistant septic shock (weak recommendation, low certainty). Corticosteroids are suggested against in fluid/vasopressor-responsive shock.
records.actionTaken: Qualified pediatric sepsis curriculum to explicitly define fluid-refractory, catecholamine-resistant criteria (≥40-60 mL/kg fluids + escalating pressors >0.2-0.3 mcg/kg/min), weight-based regimens (1-2 mg/kg/dose q6h, max 200 mg/d), anti-recommendation in responsive shock, and avoidance of adult fixed doses.
records.remainingUncertainty: Optimal dosing (intermittent 1-2 mg/kg q6h vs continuous 50-100 mg/m2/d) and tapering schedule (24 vs 48-72h) in extreme catecholamine resistance remain subject to institutional PICU protocols.

records.topic: Selective Digestive Decontamination (SDD) in ICU Infection Control
records.sourceAndEdition: SuDDICU Trial (JAMA 2022; 328(19):1911–1921); de Smet AM et al. (N Engl J Med 2009; 360:20-31); ISCCM Guidelines on Infection Control & VAP Prevention; SSC 2026 / 2021
records.notes: QUALIFIED: Distinguishes low-AMR European settings (where SDD/SOD is guideline-supported) from Indian/high-AMR ICUs (where routine enteral colistin SDD is avoided/not recommended due to colistin resistance risks, citing SuDDICU 2022 and ISCCM principles). Human clinician sign-off required for local unit policy.
records.originalClaimOrProblem: Lack of curriculum coverage distinguishing low-AMR European settings (where SDD/SOD has trial support) from high-AMR environments (including Indian ICUs) where routine enteral colistin SDD carries extreme risk of selecting pan-drug resistant pathogens.
records.reviewFinding: European trials (de Smet, NEJM 2009) in low-AMR ICUs demonstrated mortality benefits. However, the SuDDICU RCT (JAMA 2022; n=5,982) did not achieve statistically significant in-hospital mortality reduction (27.0% vs 29.1%, p=0.10). In high-AMR settings like India (>50% ESBL, high CRE/CRAB), routine enteral colistin SDD is strictly not recommended by ISCCM.
records.actionTaken: Added dedicated educational section under ICU quality bundles detailing SDD vs SOD components, European low-AMR evidence, SuDDICU trial results, and strict ISCCM non-recommendation in high-AMR/Indian practice prioritizing non-antibiotic VAE bundles.
records.remainingUncertainty: Institutional adoption of SOD vs chlorhexidine oral care in low-resistance settings remains debated; in high-resistance ICUs, potential micro-ecological shifts require clinical microbiology surveillance.

records.topic: NEET-SS CC 2024 R112 Sepsis Crystalloid Mandate Phrasing Removal
records.sourceAndEdition: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 / 2021 (Prescott HC et al., Intensive Care Med 2026; Evans L et al., Crit Care Med 2021)
records.originalClaimOrProblem: Explanation stated that Sepsis-3 bundle 'mandates minimum 30 mL/kg crystalloids'.
records.reviewFinding: SSC 2021/2026 guidelines state 30 mL/kg is a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence (suggested initial volume), not a mandate.
records.actionTaken: Replaced 'mandates minimum' with 'suggests an initial resuscitation volume of 30 mL/kg of balanced crystalloid (conditional recommendation, low certainty of evidence)'.
records.notes: Corrected explanation in criticalCare/mcqs.json to align with SSC 2026/2021 guideline strength.
